newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BZW Australia named business adviser on Telstra.
newsitem.headline: BZW Australia named business adviser on Telstra.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday said it has appointed merchant bank BZW Australia on Wednesday as its business adviser on the planned sale of a third of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp Ltd.

"The business adviser will provide independent advice to the government on all major aspects of the partial sale of Telstra and will have no selling role in the offer," Finance Minister John Fahey said in a statement announcing the appointment.
"BZW Australia brings a strong track record of advisory experience to governments on privatisations and large public share offers, both here and overseas," he said.
Fahey also announced the appointment of two legal firms to advise on the proposed sale, which expected to raise at least A$8 billion.
The government had engaged Freehill, Hollingdale and Page in Melbourne as domestic legal advisers while the U.S. firm Sullivan and Cromwell would advise on international matters, the minister said.
The engagement of the three firms constitutes the second round of appointments.
The government last month chose Australian brokers J.B. Were & Son, U.S.-based CS First Boston and Europe's ABN AMRO/Rothschild as global co-ordinators.
Fahey said the government would select accountants next.
